newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 87 n/c on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 138 -2 on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle markets continued to follow recent trends this week. Prices were softer in southern Australia but markets were reasonably firm in New South Wales and Queensland.

The Australian dollar's rise through 80 U.S. cents to a six year high, which is also up on the Japanese yen, was significant for the Australian industry. In the absence of overseas price increases, each one percent rise in the Austrsalian dollar reduces export returns to the Australian beef and sheepmeat industries by about A$30 million. This translates to about A$25.00 a head for cattle prices.
Given the soft state of overseas beef markets, most of the impact of the stronger dollar will be felt without a rise in overseas prices to offset the dollar's rise.
Futures trading suggests the dollar will remain around the 80 cents mark until the middle of next year.

The higher dollar affected returns to Australian beef exporters to the Japanese and U.S. markets this week. In the U.S., although imported manufacturing beef prices rose, returns to Australian exporters were generally lower. U.S. prices for 90CL cow beef dropped buy four cents a kg to 181 cents a kg. In Japan, prices for chilled grassfed fullsets declined 15 cents a

Japanese wholesale prices for chilled Australian grassfed beef also generally declined this week. Shortfed wholesale prices and shortfed export prices, however, were fully firm. Export prices for shortfed fullsets are currently 198 cents a kg above grassfed fullset prices.

Queensland over-the-hook prices for shortfed cattle are currently 240 cents a kg compared with a low of 155 cents a kg mid-year. However, futures contracts for Australian shortfed cattle are well below current price levels.

First signs of a decline in U.S. fed steer prices are now emerging. On Thursday evening the U.S. five market average steer price was US$69.96 a cwt, down by $2.68 a cwt from the previous Thursday. Choice grade cattle are still in reasonably short supply but select grade supplies are increasing.

With increased U.S. corn supplies prices have dropped significantly and are expected to remain well below the levels of last financial year. Simultaneously, fed cattle prices have been moving higher since mid-year.
In Japan, beef stocks for September continued to decline to 125,331 tonnes, down eight percent on the month. Stocks are still 32 percent higher than September 1995.

Reports indicate that demand is shifting from thinly sliced cuts to steak cuts. Wholesale prices of cuts in thinly-sliced dishes have been declining. Grassfed fullsets weakened on the wholesale market this week but shortfed beef is in tight supply and prices firm.
